## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1428
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1428
- **Title**: gh-1409 [GOAL] Compaction-pinned skill operative lines — instructions must survive folding (image-carrier precedent)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1409` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 36
- **Additions**: +3440
- **Deletions**: -221
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T21:40:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T05:41:04Z

## PR Description

Closes #1409
### What changed
Skills can now pin their critical instructions so they survive every compaction. A skill's `SKILL.md` accepts an `operative:` frontmatter key (numbered line ranges or `!text` needles); `SkillOperativePins.build` resolves them to byte-keyed excerpts (deduped, budget-capped, window-proportional) and the payload rides inside `CompactionManager.compact`, the structured checkpoint path, `AutoCompactor`, and the next agent turn's request — never persisted to the session JSONL and never clipped by summary sanitation.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/skills/operative_pins.dart`: resolution, dedup, char budget (min 400, 0.5% of model window) — fail-soft (`notes` list, never throws)
- Carrier is payload-only: `SystemPayloadEntry` on the outgoing request (AC1/AC8 byte-parity with compaction off)
- `summarySanitizer` promotes pinned spans (stamped `[pinned-...]` 48-hex content keys) to protection-level `exact` (AC7)
- Prompt source: `prompts/compaction/pinned_operative.md` → `pinnedOperativePrompt` (generated, drift-checked)
- Consent inheritance: a granted third-party skill's pins re-surface verbatim, prefixed with its origin marker (AC10)
- Tools window drop is bounded so the pin block can never push current-turn tools out (E9)

### How to verify
```bash
dart analyze lib test bin && dart test test/skills/ test/compaction/ test/agent/
dart test test/integration/operative_pins_e2e_test.dart   # tagged integration
```
Full suite: `dart test` (background job `sh-147-hn14qmte1710l3699` was still running at report time; all touched trees pass green individually — 538 pin tests, 124 skills, 339 compaction, 4 integration, 19 app, 32 prompts).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SK[SKILL.md operative:] --> RES[SkillOperativePins.build]
  RES -->|budget + dedup| PIN[PinnedOperativePayload]
  PIN --> CM[CompactionManager.compact]
  PIN --> SC[StructuredCompactor checkpoint]
  PIN --> AC[AutoCompactor refresh]
  CM --> REQ[Next request payload — never JSONL]
  REQ --> SAN[sanitizer: pinned spans exact]
```

</details>

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1428
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1428
- **Title**: gh-1409 [GOAL] Compaction-pinned skill operative lines — instructions must survive folding (image-carrier precedent)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1409` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 36
- **Additions**: +3440
- **Deletions**: -221
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T21:40:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T05:41:04Z

## PR Description

Closes #1409
### What changed
Skills can now pin their critical instructions so they survive every compaction. A skill's `SKILL.md` accepts an `operative:` frontmatter key (numbered line ranges or `!text` needles); `SkillOperativePins.build` resolves them to byte-keyed excerpts (deduped, budget-capped, window-proportional) and the payload rides inside `CompactionManager.compact`, the structured checkpoint path, `AutoCompactor`, and the next agent turn's request — never persisted to the session JSONL and never clipped by summary sanitation.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/skills/operative_pins.dart`: resolution, dedup, char budget (min 400, 0.5% of model window) — fail-soft (`notes` list, never throws)
- Carrier is payload-only: `SystemPayloadEntry` on the outgoing request (AC1/AC8 byte-parity with compaction off)
- `summarySanitizer` promotes pinned spans (stamped `[pinned-...]` 48-hex content keys) to protection-level `exact` (AC7)
- Prompt source: `prompts/compaction/pinned_operative.md` → `pinnedOperativePrompt` (generated, drift-checked)
- Consent inheritance: a granted third-party skill's pins re-surface verbatim, prefixed with its origin marker (AC10)
- Tools window drop is bounded so the pin block can never push current-turn tools out (E9)

### How to verify
```bash
dart analyze lib test bin && dart test test/skills/ test/compaction/ test/agent/
dart test test/integration/operative_pins_e2e_test.dart   # tagged integration
```
Full suite: `dart test` (background job `sh-147-hn14qmte1710l3699` was still running at report time; all touched trees pass green individually — 538 pin tests, 124 skills, 339 compaction, 4 integration, 19 app, 32 prompts).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SK[SKILL.md operative:] --> RES[SkillOperativePins.build]
  RES -->|budget + dedup| PIN[PinnedOperativePayload]
  PIN --> CM[CompactionManager.compact]
  PIN --> SC[StructuredCompactor checkpoint]
  PIN --> AC[AutoCompactor refresh]
  CM --> REQ[Next request payload — never JSONL]
  REQ --> SAN[sanitizer: pinned spans exact]
```

</details>

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1428
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1428
- **Title**: gh-1409 [GOAL] Compaction-pinned skill operative lines — instructions must survive folding (image-carrier precedent)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1409` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 36
- **Additions**: +3440
- **Deletions**: -221
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T21:40:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T05:41:04Z

## PR Description

Closes #1409
### What changed
Skills can now pin their critical instructions so they survive every compaction. A skill's `SKILL.md` accepts an `operative:` frontmatter key (numbered line ranges or `!text` needles); `SkillOperativePins.build` resolves them to byte-keyed excerpts (deduped, budget-capped, window-proportional) and the payload rides inside `CompactionManager.compact`, the structured checkpoint path, `AutoCompactor`, and the next agent turn's request — never persisted to the session JSONL and never clipped by summary sanitation.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/skills/operative_pins.dart`: resolution, dedup, char budget (min 400, 0.5% of model window) — fail-soft (`notes` list, never throws)
- Carrier is payload-only: `SystemPayloadEntry` on the outgoing request (AC1/AC8 byte-parity with compaction off)
- `summarySanitizer` promotes pinned spans (stamped `[pinned-...]` 48-hex content keys) to protection-level `exact` (AC7)
- Prompt source: `prompts/compaction/pinned_operative.md` → `pinnedOperativePrompt` (generated, drift-checked)
- Consent inheritance: a granted third-party skill's pins re-surface verbatim, prefixed with its origin marker (AC10)
- Tools window drop is bounded so the pin block can never push current-turn tools out (E9)

### How to verify
```bash
dart analyze lib test bin && dart test test/skills/ test/compaction/ test/agent/
dart test test/integration/operative_pins_e2e_test.dart   # tagged integration
```
Full suite: `dart test` (background job `sh-147-hn14qmte1710l3699` was still running at report time; all touched trees pass green individually — 538 pin tests, 124 skills, 339 compaction, 4 integration, 19 app, 32 prompts).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SK[SKILL.md operative:] --> RES[SkillOperativePins.build]
  RES -->|budget + dedup| PIN[PinnedOperativePayload]
  PIN --> CM[CompactionManager.compact]
  PIN --> SC[StructuredCompactor checkpoint]
  PIN --> AC[AutoCompactor refresh]
  CM --> REQ[Next request payload — never JSONL]
  REQ --> SAN[sanitizer: pinned spans exact]
```

</details>

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

content.thinking:
Confirmed. `_applySkillToggle` (CLI `/skills on|off`) calls `_resolveSkillAvailability()` + `_applyPromptComposition()` but never `_agent.operativeSkills = List.of(_enabledSkills)`. So in the CLI:

- `/skills off fleet` (disable the skill) → prompt skills index drops `fleet`, but `_agent.operativeSkills` still contains `fleet` → `injectOperativePinCarriers` keeps rebuilding the registry from the stale list → `fleet`'s pinned directives KEEP riding every post-compaction request verbatim.
- The lifecycle diff (P4/P5) won't even notice: `_buildRegistry` diffs against `lastOperativePinRegistry`, and the registry is rebuilt from the same stale skill list each time → unchanged → clean diff, notice. So the disable is silently ignored by the pin mechanism — exactly the "silent no-op / silent stale" class the round-2 review flagged on the app side, but on the toggle path of the CLI side.

Also the inverse: `/skills on fleet` on a session where fleet was disabled at boot → pins never start flowing (silent no-op) until a full `/skills reload` or restart.

This is a genuine correctness bug within the PR's own derived-state contract (P2: "consent and toggle changes re-publish"). The app host covers its toggle path; the CLI host covers reload/consent/import but NOT toggle. Severity: BLOCKING (broken behavior — a disabled skill's directives continue to be pinned into prompts; the user's explicit disable is silently ignored post-compaction). It's the same class as round-2's blocker 2 (app boot), which was accepted as BLOCKING.

Also `_reloadSkills` is called by `/skills access` (consent) — line 171? and import 419/530. Fine.

With `_messageText` allocating joined text per message per pin — actually `messages.any((m) => _messageText(m).contains(pin.line))` recomputes `_messageText(message)` for each pin! For each pin, it re-extracts text of every message until found. Worst case: pins × total window text extraction. The round-2 suggestion asked to avoid the window-sized JOIN; the fix avoids the join allocation but still re-extracts per pin. For 10 pins × 200KB window = 2MB of string extraction per request — same asymptotics the reviewer accepted ("Same asymptotics in the worst case"), so fine per the thread's resolution. Sixth: **E9 budget interplay**: in the loop, `budgetChars = min(configured, max(window ~/ 8, 1024))`. Then `SkillOperativePins.build(skills, readSkillPaths: ..., budgetChars: budgetChars)`. But `pinnedOperativePayloadOf` (auto_compactor) builds the registry WITHOUT the E9 budget — `SkillOperativePins.build(skills)` full default budget. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1428
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1428
- **Title**: gh-1409 [GOAL] Compaction-pinned skill operative lines — instructions must survive folding (image-carrier precedent)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1409` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 36
- **Additions**: +3440
- **Deletions**: -221
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T21:40:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T05:41:04Z

## PR Description

Closes #1409
### What changed
Skills can now pin their critical instructions so they survive every compaction. A skill's `SKILL.md` accepts an `operative:` frontmatter key (numbered line ranges or `!text` needles); `SkillOperativePins.build` resolves them to byte-keyed excerpts (deduped, budget-capped, window-proportional) and the payload rides inside `CompactionManager.compact`, the structured checkpoint path, `AutoCompactor`, and the next agent turn's request — never persisted to the session JSONL and never clipped by summary sanitation.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/skills/operative_pins.dart`: resolution, dedup, char budget (min 400, 0.5% of model window) — fail-soft (`notes` list, never throws)
- Carrier is payload-only: `SystemPayloadEntry` on the outgoing request (AC1/AC8 byte-parity with compaction off)
- `summarySanitizer` promotes pinned spans (stamped `[pinned-...]` 48-hex content keys) to protection-level `exact` (AC7)
- Prompt source: `prompts/compaction/pinned_operative.md` → `pinnedOperativePrompt` (generated, drift-checked)
- Consent inheritance: a granted third-party skill's pins re-surface verbatim, prefixed with its origin marker (AC10)
- Tools window drop is bounded so the pin block can never push current-turn tools out (E9)

### How to verify
```bash
dart analyze lib test bin && dart test test/skills/ test/compaction/ test/agent/
dart test test/integration/operative_pins_e2e_test.dart   # tagged integration
```
Full suite: `dart test` (background job `sh-147-hn14qmte1710l3699` was still running at report time; all touched trees pass green individually — 538 pin tests, 124 skills, 339 compaction, 4 integration, 19 app, 32 prompts).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SK[SKILL.md operative:] --> RES[SkillOperativePins.build]
  RES -->|budget + dedup| PIN[PinnedOperativePayload]
  PIN --> CM[CompactionManager.compact]
  PIN --> SC[StructuredCompactor checkpoint]
  PIN --> AC[AutoCompactor refresh]
  CM --> REQ[Next request payload — never JSONL]
  REQ --> SAN[sanitizer: pinned spans exact]
```

</details>

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

# Note: n_0992_4cd2

Running `dart test` from inside an fa harness session (this CI runner workspace) leaks the session's own FA_* env into spawned `fa` children (FA_LOG_FILE, FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE, FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG, FA_PROVIDER_TYPE, FA_SESSION_ROOT, FA_SESSION_NAME) — integration-tagged tests that spawn the CLI (headless_log_file_test, backend_mode_cli_test, headless_tools_flag_test, yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test, …) fail on assertions like "does not contain 'plain reply'" purely from that leak. CI legs run those under a clean env, so they are green there. Local fix: prefix the run with `env -u FA_LOG_FILE -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE -u FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG -u FA_PROVIDER_TYPE -u FA_SESSION_ROOT -u FA_SESSION_NAME`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1428
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1428
- **Title**: gh-1409 [GOAL] Compaction-pinned skill operative lines — instructions must survive folding (image-carrier precedent)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1409` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 36
- **Additions**: +3440
- **Deletions**: -221
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T21:40:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T05:41:04Z

## PR Description

Closes #1409
### What changed
Skills can now pin their critical instructions so they survive every compaction. A skill's `SKILL.md` accepts an `operative:` frontmatter key (numbered line ranges or `!text` needles); `SkillOperativePins.build` resolves them to byte-keyed excerpts (deduped, budget-capped, window-proportional) and the payload rides inside `CompactionManager.compact`, the structured checkpoint path, `AutoCompactor`, and the next agent turn's request — never persisted to the session JSONL and never clipped by summary sanitation.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/skills/operative_pins.dart`: resolution, dedup, char budget (min 400, 0.5% of model window) — fail-soft (`notes` list, never throws)
- Carrier is payload-only: `SystemPayloadEntry` on the outgoing request (AC1/AC8 byte-parity with compaction off)
- `summarySanitizer` promotes pinned spans (stamped `[pinned-...]` 48-hex content keys) to protection-level `exact` (AC7)
- Prompt source: `prompts/compaction/pinned_operative.md` → `pinnedOperativePrompt` (generated, drift-checked)
- Consent inheritance: a granted third-party skill's pins re-surface verbatim, prefixed with its origin marker (AC10)
- Tools window drop is bounded so the pin block can never push current-turn tools out (E9)

### How to verify
```bash
dart analyze lib test bin && dart test test/skills/ test/compaction/ test/agent/
dart test test/integration/operative_pins_e2e_test.dart   # tagged integration
```
Full suite: `dart test` (background job `sh-147-hn14qmte1710l3699` was still running at report time; all touched trees pass green individually — 538 pin tests, 124 skills, 339 compaction, 4 integration, 19 app, 32 prompts).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SK[SKILL.md operative:] --> RES[SkillOperativePins.build]
  RES -->|budget + dedup| PIN[PinnedOperativePayload]
  PIN --> CM[CompactionManager.compact]
  PIN --> SC[StructuredCompactor checkpoint]
  PIN --> AC[AutoCompactor refresh]
  CM --> REQ[Next request payload — never JSONL]
  REQ --> SAN[sanitizer: pinned spans exact]
```

</details>

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **State**: open

- **Deletions**: -221
- **Created**: 2026-10-08T21:40:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T05:41:04Z

## PR Description

Closes #1409
### What changed
Skills can now pin their critical instructions so they survive every compaction. A skill's `SKILL.md` accepts an `operative:` frontmatter key (numbered line ranges or `!text` needles); `SkillOperativePins.build` resolves them to byte-keyed excerpts (deduped, budget-capped, window-proportional) and the payload rides inside `CompactionManager.compact`, the structured checkpoint path, `AutoCompactor`, and the next agent turn's request — never persisted to the session JSONL and never clipped by summary sanitation.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/skills/operative_pins.dart`: resolution, dedup, char budget (min 400, 0.5% of model window) — fail-soft (`notes` list, never throws)
- Carrier is payload-only: `SystemPayloadEntry` on the outgoing request (AC1/AC8 byte-parity with compaction off)
- `summarySanitizer` promotes pinned spans (stamped `[pinned-...]` 48-hex content keys) to protection-level `exact` (AC7)
- Prompt source: `prompts/compaction/pinned_operative.md` → `pinnedOperativePrompt` (generated, drift-checked)
- Consent inheritance: a granted third-party skill's pins re-surface verbatim, prefixed with its origin marker (AC10)
- Tools window drop is bounded so the pin block can never push current-turn tools out (E9)

### How to verify
```bash
dart analyze lib test bin && dart test test/skills/ test/compaction/ test/agent/
dart test test/integration/operative_pins_e2e_test.dart   # tagged integration
```
Full suite: `dart test` (background job `sh-147-hn14qmte1710l3699` was still running at report time; all touched trees pass green individually — 538 pin tests, 124 skills, 339 compaction, 4 integration, 19 app, 32 prompts).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SK[SKILL.md operative:] --> RES[SkillOperativePins.build]
  RES -->|budget + dedup| PIN[PinnedOperativePayload]
  PIN --> CM[CompactionManager.compact]
  PIN --> SC[StructuredCompactor checkpoint]
  PIN --> AC[AutoCompactor refresh]
  CM --> REQ[Next request payload — never JSONL]
  REQ --> SAN[sanitizer: pinned spans exact]
```

</details>

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

# pr-1428: gh-1409 [GOAL] Compaction-pinned skill operative lines — instructions must survive folding (image-carrier precedent)

## Description

Closes #1409
### What changed
Skills can now pin their critical instructions so they survive every compaction. A skill's `SKILL.md` accepts an `operative:` frontmatter key (numbered line ranges or `!text` needles); `SkillOperativePins.build` resolves them to byte-keyed excerpts (deduped, budget-capped, window-proportional) and the payload rides inside `CompactionManager.compact`, the structured checkpoint path, `AutoCompactor`, and the next agent turn's request — never persisted to the session JSONL and never clipped by summary sanitation.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/skills/operative_pins.dart`: resolution, dedup, char budget (min 400, 0.5% of model window) — fail-soft (`notes` list, never throws)
- Carrier is payload-only: `SystemPayloadEntry` on the outgoing request (AC1/AC8 byte-parity with compaction off)
- `summarySanitizer` promotes pinned spans (stamped `[pinned-...]` 48-hex content keys) to protection-level `exact` (AC7)
- Prompt source: `prompts/compaction/pinned_operative.md` → `pinnedOperativePrompt` (generated, drift-checked)
- Consent inheritance: a granted third-party skill's pins re-surface verbatim, prefixed with its origin marker (AC10)
- Tools window drop is bounded so the pin block can never push current-turn tools out (E9)

### How to verify
```bash
dart analyze lib test bin && dart test test/skills/ test/compaction/ test/agent/
dart test test/integration/operative_pins_e2e_test.dart   # tagged integration
```
Full suite: `dart test` (background job `sh-147-hn14qmte1710l3699` was still running at report time; all touched trees pass green individually — 538 pin tests, 124 skills, 339 compaction, 4 integration, 19 app, 32 prompts).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  SK[SKILL.md operative:] --> RES[SkillOperativePins.build]
  RES -->|budget + dedup| PIN[PinnedOperativePayload]
  PIN --> CM[CompactionManager.compact]
  PIN --> SC[StructuredCompactor checkpoint]
  PIN --> AC[AutoCompactor refresh]
  CM --> REQ[Next request payload — never JSONL]
  REQ --> SAN[sanitizer: pinned spans exact]
```

</details>

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`

# Note: n_0992_4cd2

Running `dart test` from inside an fa harness session (this CI runner workspace) leaks the session's own FA_* env into spawned `fa` children (FA_LOG_FILE, FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE, FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG, FA_PROVIDER_TYPE, FA_SESSION_ROOT, FA_SESSION_NAME) — integration-tagged tests that spawn the CLI (headless_log_file_test, backend_mode_cli_test, headless_tools_flag_test, yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test, …) fail on assertions like "does not contain 'plain reply'" purely from that leak. CI legs run those under a clean env, so they are green there. Local fix: prefix the run with `env -u FA_LOG_FILE -u FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE -u FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG -u FA_PROVIDER_TYPE -u FA_SESSION_ROOT -u FA_SESSION_NAME`.

Skills can now pin their critical instructions so they survive every compaction. ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
